column1: How to use this audit workbook

column2: Instruction
Place this workbook, audit_selection.json and CODEX_PREPARE_AUDIT.txt in MVP/SHACL_GENERATION_PIPELINE/evaluation/manual_audit/AUDIT_20260915/.
Ask local Codex to package the evidence. Start with any batch and send its TXT plus the current workbook. Use Batches to track progress.
All 268 requirements prepared. BATCH_01–26 have ten each; BATCH_27 has eight. Architecture sheets each contain 268 code-review rows.
536 case IDs selected: one original expected-PASS and one expected-FAIL per requirement. The same IDs are used across architectures. No claim that two cases cover all branches.
NLTL-MANUAL-AUDIT-20260915-v1. IDs ordered by stable SHA-256; no RAND formulas. Outcome-independent random order and case selection.

RUN_01 is the only evaluated run pool supplied here. Local Codex may inventory other completed RDF-evaluated runs and sample one per architecture/requirement before any manual review. Record pool and seed, retain unsuccessful jobs, update automatic audit cells only.
Results, RawResults and RequirementScores describe RUN_01. A random code specimen from another run does not replace those outcomes. Code grades remain separate.

V2_FALLBACK25 uses accepted final outputs plus the exact 25 preserved rejected attempt-4 artifacts in the supplied diagnostic. It does not promote every parseable artifact or select best-scoring attempts.
Keep the requirement and failure status. No invented SHACL, substituted earlier attempt, or zero-filled manual grade. Mark NOT_ASSESSABLE if no chosen artifact is available.
Parse and execution fields come from recorded evidence. DETAILS_NOT_IN_PACKAGE must be filled from matching local deterministic-validation records, or remain explicitly unknown.

Amber cells accept grades, evidence and decisions. Preserve source values and row order in CaseReview, RawResults and RequirementScores: use filters, not sorting or row deletion, because their formulas link fixed evidence rows. Read Rubric before grading.

In CaseReview select LABEL_ONLY, proposed PASS/FAIL and AGREED, then reviewer, date and evidence. Effective label and all three label-adjusted RUN_01 scores update. Original labels and original Results table stay intact.

For an agreed RDF_EDIT or EXECUTION_FIX, the workbook flags RERUN_REQUIRED. It does not pretend a changed graph produced the old verdict. Reevaluate all affected saved outputs offline before importing a revised result version.
Use UNCLEAR / NEEDS_EXPERT. Do not flip a label because several models agree or because it raises a score. Establish whether code, fixture, label, interpretation, or execution is at fault.
Stable keys are architecture + requirement + selected run + artifact hash; case ID and RDF hash identify scenarios. Keep original manifest and packet hashes in the local audit folder.
Assistant suggestions are draft judgments. Record who reviewed and agreed, and retain dissent/evidence in notes. A second independent reviewer on a subset supports an agreement assessment.

Reviewing all 268 with two cases each audits selected scenarios and code evidence, not every one of the 2,186 cases. For partial review, report sample design and uncertainty; a targeted set cannot estimate the population error rate.
The packaging prompt makes no LLM calls, does not launch experiments, and does not alter rules, fixtures or original ledgers. It only assembles evidence.
For IMO26 resolve the actual supplement; the 2014 Polar Code alone is insufficient. If source text/table is missing, flag it instead of reconstructing it from an LLM.
Original figures include unavailable/error cases in the full denominator. A manual 0–2 rubric score never replaces an RDF verdict or an entire requirement’s case results.
Save new workbook versions after each completed batch, e.g. NLTL_Audit_after_BATCH_01.xlsx. Preserve the initial workbook and selection manifest.
